Subject: SIG intake — quick ask about change windows and ephemeral creds

Hi Priya / Marissa,

We are kicking off the SIG/SOC intake for Harbor Financial and the assessor has a focused ask around change windows and how you manage short-lived/ephemeral credentials in CI/CD. Can you provide a short snapshot we can include in the assessor packet? Specifically: 

- Change window policy excerpt (who can schedule out-of-band changes, approval flow)
- CI/CD runbook extract showing how we gate releases during maintenance windows
- Evidence of short-lived credential rotation (sampling of last 90 days) and the TTLs for tokens used by CI agents

Ideally we need something concise (2-3 files) by next Tuesday (2028-03-21) to keep the review on schedule. If any of this needs redaction, say so and we can accept redacted artifacts.

Thanks — if easier to sync for 20 min I can do Monday morning.

Best,
Ellen Park
Senior Security Manager, Harbor Financial
ellen.park@harborfinancial.com

2) For the rotation evidence, are logs sufficient (redacted token IDs) or do you want exported rotation events (CSV) showing issuance/expiry?
3) Are there any additional formatting requirements for the assessor (PDF vs CSV vs plain text)?

Hi Ellen / Priya — attaching the first pass artifacts. Notes in-line below.

Attachments (redacted where appropriate):
- ci-runbook.pdf (PDF) — excerpted sections: release gating, maintenance window checklist, rollback trigger points.
- shortlived-token-snapshot.csv (CSV) — sample of rotation events for CI agents (redacted token ids, timestamps, TTL).
- change-window-policy.md (MD) — excerpt covering scheduled maintenance, emergency exception approval flow, and post-change verification.

A few quick clarifications we captured while pulling these:
- Our CI agents use ephemeral tokens issued by an internal KMS-backed service. Default TTL is 15 minutes; anything that needs longer has an approval workflow and is logged.
- Change windows are scheduled via the ops calendar; emergency changes are approved by an on-call manager and require a post-change blameless review within 48 hours.
- The CSV is redacted to hide token identifiers but includes event timestamps and issuer IDs.

If you want additional log context (full audit extracts) we can provide a redacted sample, but we prefer to do that under an NDA or via a secure Drive share.

— Marissa

Hi all — looping in quick technical answers to Ellen's follow-ups. 

1) issuer_id mapping:
- ci-runner-01 -> CI agent pool (k8s worker group 'ci-runner')
- deploy-bot -> orchestration service that performs canary rollouts
- webhooks -> deployment webhook service (internal)

I will attach a small mapping table to the Drive folder.

2) post-change verification: our runbook includes a checklist with items: smoke test, log sanity, latency check, and a blameless note entry. Example steps (redacted):
- smoke: curl health endpoint /health -> expect 200 within 2s
- logs: query last 5min for ERROR > 0 -> flag
- latency: 95th percentile compare to baseline; if >20% then rollback

3) KMS/HSM rotation: we rotate symmetric keys (encryption keys) on a 12-month schedule and HSM-stored RSA signing keys every 24 months unless a key compromise or vendor advisories trigger early rotation. Ephemeral token signing uses a short-term signing key that is itself rotated on a 30-day cadence; the tokens' TTL is 15 minutes by default.

Sample CLI audit excerpt (redacted):
> $ kmscli list-issuances --service ci-runner-01 --since 2028-01-01 | head -n 5
> issuance_id,issuer_id,issued_at,expires_at,ttl
> xxxx,ci-runner-01,2028-03-10T09:12:01Z,2028-03-10T09:27:01Z,900
